rules.statement: Select or identify an elliptic curve by its identity (curve name or named-curve OID), never by inferring it from the key size in bits.
rules.why: Distinct curves can share a size (e.g. secp256k1 and P-256 are both 256-bit), so a size-keyed lookup can't generate a chosen same-size curve and will mis-identify non-NIST keys.
rules.check: Look for switches or dictionaries that map a bit length (256/384/521) to an ECCurve or curve name, used as the only way to pick or name a curve, with no lookup by name or OID.

rules.statement: When exporting an EC key as a JWK, set the `crv` value from the key's actual ECCurve (named-curve OID) and fall back to its size only when the curve can't be resolved.
rules.why: Naming `crv` from the actual curve is unambiguous. Guessing it from the size mis-names keys on curves that share a size with a NIST curve.
rules.check: Look for JWK/JWKS export code that sets `crv` from KeySize or ECParameters size alone, instead of from ECParameters.Curve.Oid or the curve's friendly name.

rules.statement: Keep a single shared source of elliptic-curve definitions for key generation, validation and JWK publication, so that no layer keeps its own separate curve table.
rules.why: When generation and publication keep separate curve registries they can drift apart. With one catalog, a newly registered curve is available everywhere at once.
rules.check: Look for a new hard-coded curve list or curve registry in generation, validation or JWKS code that duplicates the existing shared curve catalog instead of reading from it.
